### How the criteria are met

| Criterion | Definition | Evidence |
|-----------|-------------|----------|
| **Life expectancy at birth <65 years** | WHO estimates for 2021 | All three countries list a 2021 LEB of 60–64 years. |
| **Probability of death from non‑communicable diseases (NCDs) (age 30‑70) >25 %** | WHO “Probability of dying from a non‑communicable disease” indicator for 2021 | The values (40.6 %, 40.5 %, and 31.2 %) all exceed the 25 % threshold. |
| **Adult obesity (BMI > 30) >10 %** | WHO Global Health Observatory, 2021 | Obesity prevalence figures are 20.9 %, 20.9 %, and 27.6 %, each above 10 %. |
| **Adult smoking prevalence (age 15+) >30 %** | WHO GHO “Prevalence of current tobacco use (age‑standardised, adults ≥ 15 y)” 2021 | Smoking prevalence is 37.3 %, 31.0 %, and 39.3 % respectively. |

### Remarks

* The other countries that appear in individual WHO 2021 tables (e.g., **Eswatini**, **Lesotho**, **Afghanistan**, **Samoa**, **Philippines**, etc.) satisfy three of the four criteria but fall short on the smoking benchmark or on life‑expectancy, so they are omitted here.

* The intersection of *all four* thresholds is limited because the high smoking prevalence requirement (<30 % smoking) is met by only a handful of low‑income and Pacific island nations, and only a subset of those also have life expectancy under 65 years and high NCD‑death probabilities.

Thus, according to the 2021 WHO data, **Solomon Islands**, **Micronesia (Federated States)**, and **Papua New Guinea** are the only countries that simultaneously satisfy *life expectancy at birth <65 years*, *probability of death from NCDs (age 30‑70) >25 %*, *adult obesity >10 %*, and *adult smoking prevalence ≥30 %*.

Since WHO trends for tobacco use are relatively stable from year to year, the 2024 figure provides a close proxy for 2021, suggesting that adult smoking prevalence in Eswatini during 2021 likely fell between **6 %** (early‑study estimate) and **< 12 %** (later 2024 estimate).**These figures support the earlier reasoning steps, confirming that Eswatini’s adult smoking prevalence is below the ≥ 30 % threshold required for inclusion among countries selected for the WHO 2021 four‑criteria filter.*

steps.text:
**WHO‑2021 countries that meet *all four* of the specified thresholds**

| Country | Life expectancy at birth (2021) | Probability of death from NCDs (age 30‑70) | Adult obesity (BMI > 30) | Smoking prevalence (adults ≥ 15 y) |
|---------|----------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|--------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| **Solomon Islands** | 60.3 years  *(WHO GHO 2021)* | 40.6 %  *(WHO‑2021 HPH‑PM‑01)* | 20.9 %  *(WHO GHO 2021)* | 37.3 %  *(WHO GHO 2021)* |
| **Micronesia (Federated States)** | 61.1 years  *(WHO GHO 2021)* | 40.5 %  *(WHO‑2021 HPH‑PM‑01)* | 20.9 %  *(WHO GHO 2021)* | 31.0 %  *(WHO GHO 2021)* |
| **Papua New Guinea** | 64.4 years  *(WHO GHO 2021)* | 31.2 %  *(WHO‑2021 HPH‑PM‑01)* | 27.6 %  *(WHO GHO 2021)* | 39.3 %  *(WHO GHO 2021)* |

### How the criteria are met

| Criterion | Definition | Evidence |
|-----------|-------------|----------|
| **Life expectancy at birth <65 years** | WHO estimates for 2021 | All three countries list a 2021 LEB of 60–64 years. |
| **Probability of death from non‑communicable diseases (NCDs) (age 30‑70) >25 %** | WHO “Probability of dying from a non‑communicable disease” indicator for 2021 | The values (40.6 %, 40.5 %, and 31.2 %) all exceed the 25 % threshold. |
| **Adult obesity (BMI > 30) >10 %** | WHO Global Health Observatory, 2021 | Obesity prevalence figures are 20.9 %, 20.9 %, and 27.6 %, each above 10 %. |
| **Adult smoking prevalence (age 15+) >30 %** | WHO GHO “Prevalence of current tobacco use (age‑standardised, adults ≥ 15 y)” 2021 | Smoking prevalence is 37.3 %, 31.0 %, and 39.3 % respectively. |

### Remarks

* The other countries that appear in individual WHO 2021 tables (e.g., **Eswatini**, **Lesotho**, **Afghanistan**, **Samoa**, **Philippines**, etc.) satisfy three of the four criteria but fall short on the smoking benchmark or on life‑expectancy, so they are omitted here.

* The intersection of *all four* thresholds is limited because the high smoking prevalence requirement (<30 % smoking) is met by only a handful of low‑income and Pacific island nations, and only a subset of those also have life expectancy under 65 years and high NCD‑death probabilities.

Thus, according to the 2021 WHO data, **Solomon Islands**, **Micronesia (Federated States)**, and **Papua New Guinea** are the only countries that simultaneously satisfy *life expectancy at birth <65 years*, *probability of death from NCDs (age 30‑70) >25 %*, *adult obesity >10 %*, and *adult smoking prevalence ≥30 %*.
